options.content:
**SLI/SLO 101**
- SLI = the measured number (e.g. "% time waiting for CPU")
- SLO = your target threshold for that SLI (e.g. "stay under 5%")
- SLA = an SLO with contractual consequences — not relevant for a homelab

CPU pressure/throttling rule of thumb
Sustained pressure above ~5-10% is worth investigating. Below that = normal noise.

Reading a rate(x_seconds_total[...]) panel shown in ms
Raw value is a 0-1 fraction; "Seconds" unit just auto-scales it to ms/µs/ns.
Shortcut: displayed ms ÷ 10 = % (e.g. 16.51ms → 1.65%, 5.25ms → 0.5%)

### Resources/Limits — best practice
- Requests: always set (CPU + memory) — determines scheduling + QoS class. No real downside.
- Memory limits: always set — memory is incompressible; contains a leak/spike to just that container instead of destabilizing the node.
- CPU limits: debated in big clusters (CFS quota can throttle even with spare node capacity) — but on small hardware (4 cores/node), still worth setting, sized generously above observed peaks, since one runaway container can starve everything else here.

### Where resources actually live
- Container level only — containers[].resources
- Pod: pod.spec.containers[].resources
- Deployment/StatefulSet/etc: spec.template.spec.containers[].resources (same field, nested via the pod template)
- Service: never — pure networking, no compute concept at all
- Multi-container pod = each container gets its own independent resources block; pod total = sum of all containers

### QoS Classes — determined automatically by what you set
- Guaranteed: requests == limits (for every container, both CPU and memory) — highest priority, last to be evicted under node pressure.
- Burstable: requests < limits (at least one resource set, not equal) — normal default choice, what most of your apps use.
- BestEffort: no requests/limits set at all — first to be evicted under node pressure, first to get OOM-killed. What every app had before you started this resource-tuning pass.

Class is never set directly — it's a pure side effect of the requests/limits values you declare per container.
